🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-08-29 23:00 → 2026-08-30 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **ERC-8183 reached formal-draft stage with independent external verification** — A PR review re-ran an independent external profile to confirm the spec still holds, giving the group concrete external evidence at this key milestone. [tg:tawg:3744]

> **ERC-8354 programKey derivation and rotation loop closed in agent-sdk** — Back-to-back commits wired programKey to VK_HASH, introduced verifier rotation, and emitted the canonical domain event, completing a full spec-to-code cycle. [commit 902b448e](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-sdk/commit/902b448e0e71c23996d0fd27a2f187c47354071e)

> **CAPV interfaces synced with the merged ERC-8354 spec** — A new PR aligns contract interfaces with the already-merged normative text, preventing implementation drift right at the merge boundary. [PR #19](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-ercs/pull/19)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### agent-sdk
_ERC-8354 implementation advanced through a focused chain of commits and a CI gate that closed a clear spec-to-code loop._

- Baby Blue Viper **Derived** programKey from VK_HASH and hardened regression tests as the first follow-up to the spec merge, establishing a reproducible correctness anchor that future verifier work can rely on. [commit 6c7a517](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-sdk/commit/6c7a51749ba115fda18eb04f2eb1c54404124895)

- Baby Blue Viper **Completed** the rotation follow-up by introducing verifier rotation, emitting the canonical domain event on each rotation, and restoring interface byte-identity, giving downstream consumers a stable, spec-compliant surface. [commit 902b448e](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-sdk/commit/902b448e0e71c23996d0fd27a2f187c47354071e)

- Baby Blue Viper **Opened** PR #27 to gate the full go/test package and explicitly disclose the real-proof coverage boundary, making CI feedback reliable and transparent for every future contributor. [PR #27](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-sdk/pull/27)

- Jimmy Shi **Reviewed** PR #26 by acknowledging the careful reproduction work and keeping the expiry limitation explicitly visible, giving the team a transparent view of what remains before full coverage is reached. [PR #26 comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-sdk/pull/26#issuecomment-5469446792)

### ERC-8183
_The spec review direction advanced to formal-draft stage, grounded by independent external verification._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Posted** a substantive PR review and re-ran a second independent external profile to confirm the spec still holds, supplying concrete external evidence at the formal-draft milestone. [tg:tawg:3744]

- Pavlo **Acknowledged** Baby Blue Viper's independent recomputation of the Nostr event id and signature on the Ethereum Magicians thread, reinforcing the verification result publicly for the broader community. [Magicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/398)

### ERC-8354 discussion
_The conceptual boundary around programKey was articulated precisely, aligning shared vocabulary with the ongoing implementation work._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Clarified** that the ERC-8354 programKey example cleanly shows how a deterministic procedure can be reproduced exactly while remaining conceptually bounded, giving the group a precise shared framing for spec and implementation discussions going forward. [tg:tawg:3747]

### agent-ercs
_Interface alignment with the merged spec moved forward through a concrete PR._

- Zidan **Opened** PR #19 to sync CAPV contract interfaces with the merged ERC-8354 spec, reducing the risk of normative drift and making implementation easier to verify against the standard. [PR #19](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-ercs/pull/19)

### organization
_Group coordination and new arrivals kept collective context and momentum growing._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Flagged** the RVR proposal PR for a Trusty knowledge update, helping keep the group's shared reference current with active spec work. [tg:tawg:3755]

- Merlini (@gobross) **Checked in** ready for another day of collaborative work, sustaining the daily engagement that keeps the group's rhythm strong. [tg:tawg:3764]

- Logan Verdict (@loganverdict) **Joined** the group, bringing a new community member into the shared effort advancing the Trustless AI goal. [tg:tawg:3779]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- The RVR proposal PR Jimmy Shi flagged is worth examining alongside ERC-8354 for conceptual and interface overlap
- Pavlo's framing of the deterministic-reproducibility boundary may be worth capturing in formal spec commentary

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Review and provide feedback on PR #19 to advance the CAPV interface sync
- Address items noted as outstanding in the PR #26 review before closing the coverage gap
- Process the knowledge update for RVR to keep Trusty's reference aligned with active spec work

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A boundary named in discussion — that a deterministic procedure can be reproduced exactly yet remain conceptually bounded — became a chain of implementation commits and a CI gate before the day closed, completing a loop from shared vocabulary to shipped code.
>
> When your spec vocabulary ships as a CI gate the same day it's named, the pipeline isn't just running — it's basically frictionless. Keep the loop tight! 🔄
